audit.whatIsWrong: Bramble Smash carries grounding — Riot's shockwave knocks back and slows, and the kit flags it grounding. Unstoppable Force is a dash. The entry says level 6 gives Malphite pressure Maokai 'simply can't answer'.
audit.why: He can answer it, with a 7s cooldown. Grounding shuts off dashes, so a Maokai holding Bramble Smash can take your 130s ultimate off you before it leaves. That inverts the level-6 advice from 'he has no answer' to 'spend his Q first, then commit', which is the difference between banking an ult and wasting one for two minutes.
audit.corrected: Bramble Smash grounds on a 7s cooldown — bait it before you commit Unstoppable Force.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance is called 'his W root-dash' three times and its untargetability is never mentioned. Riot: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target.'
audit.why: A reader who sees the dash start and answers with Seismic Shard or Ground Slam spends the cooldown on nothing, and is then rooted with both buttons down. The correct play is to hold Ground Slam for the moment he arrives and the root lands, not for the dash.
audit.corrected: He is untargetable through Twisted Advance — hold your answer for the landing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sap Magic's refresh condition is absent. Riot: 'Maokai's basic attack also heals him and deals additional damage on a moderate cooldown. Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced.'
audit.why: This is the one line that changes how you poke him. Chipping a Maokai with spells is not free — every Seismic Shard and Ground Slam you land accelerates the heal you are trying to out-damage. It also makes Grievous Wounds the item that decides the extended trades this entry keeps recommending, and anti-heal is mentioned nowhere.
audit.corrected: Every spell you land shortens Sap Magic's heal cooldown; bring Grievous Wounds.

audit.whatIsWrong: late says 'He'll try to match your engage with his own R knockback, but your Unstoppable Force has the longer range'. Nature's Grasp is a rooting wall at 3000 range; Unstoppable Force is 1000.
audit.why: Both halves are wrong and they compound. His ult roots rather than knocks back, and it reaches three times further than yours, so the claim that you choose the fight is exactly backwards — he opens from outside your engage range and you arrive already rooted.
audit.corrected: Nature's Grasp is a 3000-range rooting wall against your 1000-range R; he opens, not you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart marks levels 2 and 3 as Malphite while whys[1] says 'His Q knockback and sapling stack still out-chip you before W/E — hold under tower' and whys[2] says 'Maokai edges level 3'. The full layer's chart for the same matchup gives Skill at level 2 and Maokai at level 3.
audit.why: The chart contradicts the sentence printed directly under it, in both directions, and the full layer already has it right. Bringing the content chart to Skill and Maokai reconciles all three without touching the stages the 52.71% justifies.
audit.corrected: win[1] Malphite to Skill, win[2] Malphite to Maokai.
sources: packet malphite.json (maokai levelChart: Skill, Skill, Maokai, Malphite...)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] presents level 6 as an unanswerable swing.
audit.why: The spike is real but conditional on his Bramble Smash being spent. Stating the condition is what makes the spike usable rather than a trap.
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike restated with the grounding condition attached.

edits.before: Stack armor so W empowered autos and E Ground Slam out-trade his even-trading kit
edits.after: Bring Grievous Wounds early — every spell you land refreshes his Sap Magic heal

edits.before: Land his W root-dash to lock you for a sapling-stacked trade or to set up his jungler
edits.after: Twisted Advance goes untargetable mid-dash, so your Q and E both answer nothing

edits.before: Match your engage with his own R knockback and drag the lane to a slow even scale
edits.after: Ground your Unstoppable Force with Bramble Smash (Q, 7s) before it ever leaves

edits.before: Unstoppable Force gives you all-in and gank-setup pressure Maokai can't match — your single biggest swing.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is your swing, but Bramble Smash grounds — bait his 7s Q before you commit the dash.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force gives you all-in and gank-setup pressure his reactive R can't match — your biggest spike.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is your biggest spike, yet Bramble Smash grounds it — spend his 7s Q first, then commit.

edits.before: Once W Thunderclap and E Ground Slam are online you stabilize fast — your empowered autos and armor stack let you farm straight through his sapling poke, and Maokai has no way to punish a tank who out-sustains him. Level 6 is your swing: Unstoppable Force gives you all-in and gank-setup pressure he simply can't answer, since his own R is reactive peel, not a flank. Bait his W root, dodge or eat it on minions, then look to R him into your jungler.
edits.after: Once Thunderclap and Ground Slam are online you stabilize fast — empowered autos and an armor stack let you farm straight through Sapling Toss chip. Level 6 is your swing with one caveat: Bramble Smash grounds, so a Maokai holding Q strips Unstoppable Force before it leaves. Bait the 7s Q, then commit. Never answer Twisted Advance mid-dash either — he is untargetable through it, so hold Ground Slam for the moment the root lands and R him into your jungler.

edits.before: This stays yours — Maokai is a low-damage utility tank with no percent-HP or true damage to reclaim the lane, so your armor and HP stacking only pull further ahead. He'll try to match your engage with his own R knockback, but your Unstoppable Force has the longer range and you choose the fight. Stack armor, flank a carry with R, and let your team clean up while his peel does nothing to a frontline that out-trades him 1v1.
edits.after: This stays yours on stats — no percent-HP or true damage on his kit, so armor and HP stacking pull you further ahead. Two corrections though. Nature's Grasp is a rooting wall at 3000 range against your 1000-range R, so he opens the fight, not you — respect the angle. And Sap Magic's heal cooldown drops every time he casts or eats a spell, so your own poke feeds it: buy Grievous Wounds before you commit to grinding him down.

notes: Three genuinely decisive facts were missing and one was stated backwards. Bramble Smash grounds on a 7s cooldown and Unstoppable Force is a dash, so 'level 6 is a swing he can't answer' was false — he answers it with a basic ability. Twisted Advance makes him untargetable through the dash, so spells thrown at the dash are wasted. Sap Magic's heal cooldown is reduced every time he casts or is struck by a spell, which means Malphite's own poke accelerates the sustain he is trying to beat, and anti-heal appeared nowhere. Reversed: Nature's Grasp is a 3000-range rooting wall, not a knockback, and it out-ranges Unstoppable Force three to one, so the claim that Malphite chooses the fight is wrong. Not asserted: whether grounding applied mid-flight stops an Unstoppable Force already travelling, or only prevents the cast.
